Science.summary: A study on how select species of rays and sharks respond to sensory deterrents has reinforced why there isn't a one-size-fits-all solution to prevent fisheries bycatch.

Science.title: Mathematics fact fluency interventions for students with mathematics difficulties
Science.summary: Associate professor Jonté Myers knows that developing fluency with mathematics facts is key to mathematics proficiency. However, many students struggle to develop these foundational skills.

Science.title: Dinosaurs likely tore meat like birds of prey
Science.summary: Meat-eating dinosaurs probably fed by dragging their teeth backward through flesh like a saw rather than biting straight down like a dagger, new experiments suggest.

Science.title: Early Stone Age rock carvings in Scandinavia may have been signposts for hunting grounds
Science.summary: Between roughly 9,000 and 4,000 B.C., artists in ancient Scandinavia painstakingly carved large, sometimes life-size images of elk, reindeer, bears and other creatures into rock faces teetering on the edge of fjords, rivers and lakes. But their meaning has long been debated.

Science.title: God-faced rings may have identified Mesoamerica's long-distance merchants
Science.summary: Over 1,000 years ago, a Mesoamerican may have been traveling through foreign lands. Upon arriving at his destination, he held up his hand, adorned with a ring showing the face of a god, but what was this ring's purpose?

Science.title: Do we really know more about space than the ocean?
Science.summary: New discoveries are made about the world every day—a species of deep-sea fish here, a new galaxy there. There's a saying, "We know more about space than the ocean." But is this true? How do we determine knowing? Is it the number of things we have directly observed, or is it a matter of resolution?

Science.title: Wave-like displays in animal groups may have evolved to deceive predators
Science.summary: Some of the most striking patterns in collective behavior emerge in the face of danger. When a predator approaches, some animal groups morph into a vision of pulsing waves. These patterns might be more than a side effect of group living; they could have evolved as a form of deception, argue Dr. Eduardo Sampaio and professor Iain Couzin of the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior (MPI-AB) and the University of Konstanz in a Perspectives piece published in Science.

Science.title: Rocket Lab sending Japanese satellite to orbit on Thanksgiving Day launch: Watch it live
Science.summary: The Thanksgiving Day launch will be Rocket Lab's 14th mission for Tokyo-based Synspective, its largest customer.

Science.title: Sending an Australian astronaut to space is expensive. How do we work out if it's worth it?
Science.summary: Australia is currently in talks with the European Space Agency (ESA) over potentially flying Katherine Bennell-Pegg on a future space mission. If accepted, Bennell-Pegg—who is the director of space technology at the Australian Space Agency and completed ESA training in 2024—would become the first officially funded Australian astronaut.

Science.title: Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video)
Science.summary: The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Tortillas, hot sauce and pasta are on the menu, at least for one of them.

Science.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
Science.summary: Your guide to December's full Cold Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
